prompt: Move the knight to fork the black king and the rook.

feedback.default: That's a legal knight move, but it doesn't attack both the king and the rook. Look for the square where the knight's L-shape lines up with both pieces at once.

successExplanation: Ne5 forks the king on g6 (check!) and the rook on c6 at the same time — the rook falls next move.

prompt: Move the knight to fork the black king and the queen, not just give check.

feedback.default: A knight move that only checks the king isn't the goal here — you're looking for the square that attacks the king AND the queen at the same time.

successExplanation: Nd5 forks the king on e7 and the queen on c7 — a much bigger prize than a plain check.

prompt: One of Black's pieces is hanging — capture it.

feedback.default: That doesn't win any material. Which black piece is attacked and has no defender at all?

successExplanation: Rxd4 wins the knight for free — nothing defended it.

feedback.default: That doesn't capture anything hanging. Which square can your knight jump to that lands on an undefended black piece?

successExplanation: Nxc3 wins the knight — nothing was defending it.

prompt: Develop a minor piece instead of rushing your queen out.

feedback.default: That's not a developing move for a minor piece yet. Bring a knight or bishop out before touching the queen.

successExplanation: Nf3 develops a piece toward the center and prepares to castle — no target for Black's minor pieces to attack.

prompt: Develop your kingside bishop instead of moving the queen out early.

feedback.default: That's not developing the bishop. Bring it out to an active diagonal before the queen enters the game.

successExplanation: Bc4 develops the bishop onto an active diagonal, eyeing f7 — a much sounder plan than an early queen move.
